title: Founder info hazards: feeds, LLM sycophancy and staying grounded
summary: Dalton Caldwell and PB discuss how feeds and LLMs can distort a founder's thinking, drawing on Dalton's FriendFeed experience creating the like button. The fix is limits, gaps away from screens, and grounding in real people and real customers who say no to your product.

principles.text: Cap time on feeds; most value comes early and harm accumulates with doom scrolling.
principles.quote: I feel like I get the most value in the first 10 minutes. But then like the most harm is done

principles.text: Feeds are sand that crowds out substance; you must cut yourself off because they have no end.
principles.quote: if you take too much, there's there's no room for anything of substance. And so, a lot of times, the hardest thing is just cutting yourself off

principles.text: Don't use LLMs or social platforms as a mirror to judge who you are.
principles.quote: not ever holding up these technologies is a mirror of yourself.

principles.text: Be wary of LLMs validating big life decisions or grand claims, since they affirm rather than push back.
principles.quote: be especially um wary of the LLM validating big life decisions or [clears throat] fantastical claims not backed in reality about your abilities.

principles.text: Take regular gaps away from these tools to come up for air; a good test is whether you can disconnect.
principles.quote: Having gaps where you essentially come up for air, I think is is pretty essential

principles.text: Selling is grounding: asking for money exposes whether everyone really wants your product.
principles.quote: actually trying to sell products is is a form of grounding. Because when you ask people for money, they say no.
